### J-1 Appending a fix task withdraws the tasks approval the implement stage needs
- quote: "exit 0 when the tasks gate is approved or closed by the human on the current tasks, plan and spec"
- quote: "the implement stage (#43) calls this before it claims a task"
- quote: "after `nio: approve tasks`, a planned task whose text changed fails, naming it, and says "planned tasks are frozen after approval""
- quote: "if current != judged:"
- situation (architecture-fit): The existing jury hashes the whole gate artefact (`artefact` joins every file in `GATES[gate]`). `compose` returns `rerun` whenever the current blob differs from the judged one. CT-12 puts `tasks.md` in that artefact. When the implementation jury appends T-12 under `#### Fixes`, which FR-27 and FR-50 allow after approval, `approved()` turns false. The implement stage then refuses to claim T-12 or any other task until the tasks jury re-runs. Meanwhile CT-16 treats appending below `#### Fixes` as legal without re-approval.
- fix: Have CT-14 judge approval on the planned part of `tasks.md` plus the plan and spec, for example the text above each `#### Fixes`, with CT-16's frozen check guarding it. Otherwise state that every fix task needs a new tasks-jury round and a new `nio: approve tasks` commit, and test that in TC-53 and TC-40.
- validation: confirmed: CT-12 puts tasks.md in the gate artefact and CT-14 asks for approval "on the current tasks". The existing jury hashes the whole artefact, so appending a fix task under `#### Fixes` (legal per CT-16) turns `approved()` false. Nothing in the plan excludes the Fixes section from the hash.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-12: the tasks artefact leaves out each Fixes section, so approval covers planned tasks, plan and spec; CT-14 says a fix task appended since doesn't withdraw it (FR-27, FR-50)

### J-2 US-7 delivers nothing that can refuse a state transition, yet its tests expect refusals
- quote: "#45 supplies `states` and enforces the transitions"
- quote: "`finished(states, epic) -> (bool, not_done)`"
- quote: "T-3's state stays green; the message names the missing review."
- quote: "are tested through `tasks.finished` and `tasks.approved`, which those stages will call"
- situation (architecture-fit): TC-58, TC-43 and TC-44 cover CT-15 and assert that a "set to done" or a claim is refused, with messages. CT-15 is a pure predicate over a states dict, and it explicitly leaves transitions to #45. No contract in the plan holds a state or emits "dependencies not done" or "already claimed". When US-7 is done, the only things to show are `finished()` on a dict and a ledger path that `jury.load` already produces. The three refusal ACs cannot pass from what is built.
- situation (test-proof): CT-15 only reports whether an epic is finished, and this plan builds nothing that claims, moves or refuses a task. TC-43, TC-44 and TC-58 can't run against any code here. If a test stubs a refusal itself, a state table that allows claimed → done would pass. The plan decision says these go through `tasks.finished`, but `finished` emits neither "already claimed" nor "missing review".
- fix: Either move AC-36, AC-56 and AC-57 (and their TCs) to wait on #45, as the spec's non-goal says ("AC-29, AC-30, AC-36 and AC-55 to AC-57 run once #45 and #43 are built"), and say so in `## Decisions`. Or add a contract that owns the transition table, so US-7 has something to show.
- validation: confirmed: CT-15 is only `finished(states, epic)` and leaves transitions to #45. No contract in the plan produces "dependencies not done", "already claimed" or "missing review", yet US-7 owns TC-58, TC-43 and TC-44, which assert those refusals. The plan's Decisions line does not close the gap, because `finished` does not refuse anything.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: TC-43, TC-44 and TC-58 move to tests/test_flow.py and run once #45 builds nio flow, as the spec's non-goal says; the Decisions line now says so

### J-3 CT-11 promises executability alone, but the bound `jury.plan` adds spec-gate risk lenses and the scope lens to any non-plan gate
- quote: "`nio jury plan <slug> tasks` → `lenses: executability (core)`"
- quote: "if flags & set(risk) and (lens in PLAN_TRIGGERED if gate == "plan" else not at_plan):"
- quote: "elif spec.SCOPE_NOTE in notes[0]:"
- quote: "Tasks-jury lenses beyond executability, and the plan-gate coverage checks (#28, #50)."
- situation (architecture-fit): In the existing `plan()`, any gate other than `plan` takes the spec branch. On a spec flagged `auth` or `money`, the tasks gate would schedule the spec-gate risk lenses. It would also test `spec.SCOPE_NOTE` against `notes[0]` of the tasks check, whose notes CT-4 never defines, and an empty list raises IndexError. CT-11 says neither that these branches are excluded nor how the tasks gate gets its own branch, and it does not mention `CORE["tasks"]`, which architecture.md names.
- fix: In CT-11's Shape, state that the tasks gate adds `CORE["tasks"] = ["executability"]`, runs `tasks.check` in its own branch, and skips the risk-lens and scope triggers. Add a TC with a risk-flagged spec that asserts only executability is planned.
- validation: confirmed: `jury.plan` has an `else` branch for every gate other than plan. It calls `spec.check` and applies the spec-gate risk lenses, then tests `spec.SCOPE_NOTE in notes[0]`. CT-11 does not mention `CORE["tasks"]`, a tasks branch, or excluding those triggers. CT-4 defines no notes for the tasks check.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-11: CORE[tasks] = executability, its own branch in jury.plan running tasks.check, no risk or scope lens; TC-24 uses a risk-flagged spec and asserts only executability

### J-4 CT-13 binds `jury.load`, but the change it needs is a `GATES` entry whose file list it defers
- quote: "`jury.GATES` accepts any `implementation-E-<n>` name, its files set by #29"
- quote: "for n in GATES[gate]"
- quote: "raise ValueError(f"gate must be one of {sorted(GATES)}")"
- quote: "The implementation jury records round 1 on E-2."
- situation (architecture-fit): `load`, `folder` and `verdict` already derive `jury/<gate>.json` and the subject `<gate>:<slug>` from any name, so the bound symbol needs no change. `collect` rejects any gate not in `GATES`, and `artefact` and `sources` index `GATES[gate]` for a file list. A pattern name with no files is not something `GATES`, a dict of file lists, can hold. TC-60 needs a round recorded, which needs `collect`. Either TC-60 cannot pass in this feature, or the implementer must invent the file list that the contract assigns to #29.
- situation (test-proof): `jury.load`, `save` and `verdict` already accept any gate name, write `<gate>.json` and `.md`, and set the subject to `<gate>:<slug>`. If the ledger is written through them, TC-60 passes before CT-13 is built. The real gap is that `collect` still raises "gate must be one of" for `implementation-E-2`, and the test doesn't touch that.
- fix: Rebind CT-13 to what actually changes (`jury.GATES` lookup / `collect`) and give a concrete file list for an `implementation-E-n` gate. Otherwise mark CT-13 as having no code change (paths already follow the gate name) and move TC-60 to #29.
- validation: confirmed: `collect` raises "gate must be one of" for any gate not in `GATES`, and `artefact` indexes `GATES[gate]`. CT-13 binds `jury.load`, which needs no change, and defers the file list to #29. TC-60 cannot go green through `collect` in this feature.
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-13 binds jury.verdict, which already gives the path and subject from the gate name; collecting implementation-E-n rounds is #29's. TC-60 pins the existing behaviour

### J-5 CT-7 changes `resolve`'s return without its callers, and `resolve` is keyed by card name while TC-48 needs it for a task
- quote: "`resolve(cfg, name, meta, host)` returns the nearest lower mapped tier's model and a warning naming the tier and the model used"
- quote: """"(tier, model or None, effort) for a card on a host, after config overrides.""""
- quote: "_, want, _ = resolve(cfg, name, cards[name][0], "claude")"
- quote: "Setup: A task with `Tier: frontier` and a Claude host."
- situation (architecture-fit): `sync` and `verify` unpack a 3-tuple from `resolve`. `sync` builds its own "inherits the parent's" warning when no model is mapped. CT-7 adds a warning to the return value but says nothing about either caller. `verify` would then compare against a model computed differently from the one `sync` rendered. `resolve` also applies `agents.override` by card `name`, and a task's worker in TC-48 has no card name.
- fix: In CT-7's Shape, state the new return (e.g. `(tier, model, effort, warning)`), that `sync` prints the warning in place of its inherit message, and that `verify` uses the same fallback. Also say how a task's tier reaches `resolve` (e.g. `name=None`, no override), or bind TC-48 to the implement stage (#43).
- disposition: plan-fix by agent: CT-7: resolve returns (tier, model, effort, warning); sync prints the warning and verify uses the same model; a task calls it with name=None
